title: Streetlight repair intake and operator-assisted routing
brief: I need a system for a small city team to handle streetlight repair requests: classify reports, find existing tickets and route to the right maintenance crew. Five operators handle about 200 reports a day. It must not remotely control equipment.

assumptions.statement: Proposed first release ingests text typed or pasted by an operator, plus optional asset ID/address; direct citizen-channel integration, photo interpretation and ticket closure are deferred.
assumptions.why: A usable bounded release requires no invented channel contract.
assumptions.validation: Confirm intake channels and observe a shift; agree excluded formats.

assumptions.statement: A city-scoped ticket ledger, GIS asset registry and versioned crew routing table can provide read APIs; create-ticket and attach-report commands require a verified adapter.
assumptions.why: The brief names no actual systems or available APIs.
assumptions.validation: Obtain sandbox schemas and demonstrate reads, conditional writes, durable idempotency lookup and report uniqueness. If unavailable run read-only assist only.

assumptions.statement: Each ticket write requires a currently authorized operator approval; tenant is city ID, and operation, resource, report revision, immutable payload digest and policy version are bound to approval.
assumptions.why: Unknown city authority defaults to no autonomous write.
assumptions.owner: City service owner and IT security lead
assumptions.validation: Approve role matrix, routing authority and API-side checks; test revocation and cross-city denial.

assumptions.statement: Potential exposed wires, fallen poles, sparks or fire enter a staffed urgent manual queue immediately; proposed acknowledgement 2 elapsed minutes and supervisor escalation at 2 minutes; routine exceptions acknowledge within 30 staffed minutes and escalate at 30.
assumptions.why: Safety routing and real out-of-hours coverage must be agreed locally; these are proposed timers, not emergency advice.
assumptions.validation: Sign off local emergency procedure, staffed calendar, fallback contact and coverage; drill overdue/out-of-hours delivery.

assumptions.statement: Suggested duplicates require operator selection of an existing ticket on the same asset; fuzzy similarity never merges or suppresses reports. Existing ticket links do not change crew assignment or close work.
assumptions.why: Different faults or repaired/reopened work can resemble one another.
assumptions.validation: Review same-asset recurrence and multi-fault examples; verify link behavior in sandbox.

assumptions.statement: Proposed data policy: redact reporter contact before LLM use; raw local intake expires after 30 days, recommendation snapshots after 90 days, minimal audit receipts after 365 days; residency and legal retention require city approval.
assumptions.why: The brief supplies no privacy or records policy.
assumptions.validation: Approve retention/residency and deletion exceptions before real records; validate deletes and audit integrity.

assumptions.statement: Proposed routing uses a versioned GIS boundary, asset ownership, fault category and crew capability/on-duty table; unresolved boundary, unavailable crew or conflicting asset evidence goes to supervisor.
assumptions.why: No crew jurisdiction or roster is supplied.
assumptions.validation: Publish authoritative policy version and validate boundary/roster samples with crews.

assumptions.statement: Illustrative planning: 90% of reports reach the single LLM component, 5% of those need one format/transient retry, 2000 input and 300 output tokens/call, USD 1/input-million and 4/output-million; provider and actual prices remain unselected.
assumptions.why: Budget must be reproducible without invented provider facts.
assumptions.validation: Measure branch mix, context length, latency and quoted prices on approved provider. No spend authorized.

assumptions.statement: Proposed gates: zero unauthorized/wrong-city/equipment operations and zero duplicate records in synthetic controls; urgent recall at least 99% on adjudicated offline set; routine routing agreement at least 95%; active handling-time reduction target 20% relative to baseline.
assumptions.why: Thresholds are hypotheses for review, not measured results or accepted residual risk.
assumptions.validation: Approve thresholds and powered evaluation before pilot; no safety breach can be averaged away.

assumptions.statement: Proposed operational limits: each read attempt 5 seconds, one read retry; LLM attempt 10 seconds with one retry; ticket write timeout 5 seconds with zero automatic write retry; reconciliation reads at 5, 30 and 120 seconds, then owned unknown hold with 15-minute read-only watchdog. Proposed additional limits: snapshot age at plan creation 60 seconds, plan/approval expiry 5 elapsed minutes, routine nonhuman response p95 30 seconds, and unknown-held >1 hour escalates service manager. These limits require verification, not established policy.
assumptions.why: Bounded behavior and human ownership are required for implementability.
assumptions.validation: Verify latency/capacity, idempotency retention and unknown-commit support in sandbox.

assumptions.statement: Proposed measurement uses two representative working weeks of baseline/shadow and two working weeks of randomized pilot, extending to the power-analysis requirement; no sample size or savings are established. Proposed assist usability phase lasts one working week; live pilot is one approved crew area and remains operator-confirmed.
assumptions.why: 200 reports/day is volume, not evidence of statistical power.
assumptions.validation: Estimate handling-time variance, within-operator correlation, strata prevalence and cluster-adjusted sample size.

items.title: Case journal, owner timers and status projection
items.description: Durable local transaction saves terminal status plus reason, ownerRole, ackDueAt/nextReadAt, operation linkage, receipt and audit. Statuses: COMPLETED, CANCELLED_PROPOSAL, OWNED_MANUAL, UNKNOWN_HELD. COMPLETED requires actual C6/C7 receipt and means ticket action recorded, never equipment repaired. Urgent and ordinary queue entries notify only internal configured console; out-of-hours delivery contract must be verified before launch. Owner ACK does not close case. Timer persists after operator logout, overdue changes owner to duty supervisor, then at another 2 urgent elapsed/30 routine staffed minutes escalate service manager console. Reconciliation outage also escalates IT operations. Manual outcomes are recorded resolution events; cannot fabricate ticket receipt. Unknown holds freeze fresh writes for same businessKey; watchdog creates W7 read-only reconciliation instance, never restarts W1. Before-send cancellation wins if CAS before journal MAY_HAVE_SENT; after that freeze and reconcile. Input reason mapping is exact upstream C1/C2/C3/C4/C5/C6 reason string; C7 NOT_COMMITTED maps WRITE_NOT_COMMITTED, UNKNOWN maps COMMIT_UNKNOWN, AUTH_DENIED maps RECOVERY_AUTH_DENIED, INVALID_CALLBACK maps INVALID_CALLBACK. W9/W10 explicitly dispatch failed finalization; their terminal projection nodes are idempotent no-op reads of already saved status. Urgent ackDueAt is intake.receivedAt + 2 elapsed minutes even when model/retrieval took time; routine due is queueCreatedAt + 30 staffed minutes using the frozen calendar version. Retention worker runs daily with data-owner-approved versioned H6 policy; removes restricted raw data at day 30 and recommendation snapshots at day 90, minimizes audit until day 365, emits deletion receipts.
